PullRequest.Title: test: preserve WSL import failure diagnostics
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- Capture the decoded WSL2 import output, exit code, installer result, Windows/WSL versions, partial import files, and bounded WSL/Host Compute/Hyper-V events when the smoke-test distro import fails.
- Save diagnostics under `.build/logs/wsl-dev-container/` before cleanup removes the partial import, so existing CI logs artifacts preserve the evidence.
- Leave WSL installation, retry, and cleanup behavior unchanged.

Motivated by the [Windows Electron setup failure in build 476284](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_build/results?buildId=476284&view=logs&j=15ec5277-fdc6-550c-b203-acb65f44f31c&t=95193302-a421-588f-30a2-3600268fa4c0), where `wsl --import --version 2` returned `0x80041001` without enough evidence to identify the cause.

## Validation
- PowerShell parser reports no errors.
- Exercised `Write-WslDiagnostics` locally without importing a distro; verified the persisted log contains the required sections.
- `git diff --check` passed.

A Windows CI run is needed to validate the failure path on a hosted agent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful WSL smoke-test provisioning through the distro import
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing kernel installer and single `wsl.exe --import` subprocess must complete before provisioning continues. The diff records the start time and captures the import's native output before replaying it; no new subprocess, filesystem scan, IPC, or network operation is placed on the successful critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for `msiexec.exe`, then execute one `wsl.exe --import` of the pinned Ubuntu rootfs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one installer and one import per setup run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same installer and one synchronous WSL import ran before the diff; the diff only logs the installer exit code and captures/replays the import output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must complete before the smoke environment can progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Captured allocation scales with lines emitted by one `wsl --import`; this command is normally silent or emits only a small status/error message, independent of rootfs bytes processed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One setup invocation runs the installer and import serially; there is no parallel fan-out or queueing change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in import execution. The downloaded archive and setup directory are per-run, and the changed output capture has no cold/warm distinction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the boundary count and serialization are unchanged; only small command output is newly retained until import completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact native output varies by installed WSL version, but there is no evidence of realistically large import output or an added boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the success path adds only bounded output buffering and logging around an unchanged single import.

Scenarios.Scenario: Failed WSL distro import and diagnostic artifact collection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the unchanged import returns nonzero, diagnostics run serially before the script throws, so their work delays only terminal failure reporting and artifact preservation, not successful provisioning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the failed import once, then collect WSL version, status, and distribution-list output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One failed import; one `wsl --version` query newly added, plus the pre-existing one status and one list query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The failed import was followed by `wsl --status` and `wsl --list --verbose`; it did not query `wsl --version`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The version query adds one small subprocess only after setup has already failed; status/list were already on this failure path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate the top level of the partial install directory and create/append the import diagnostics log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One non-recursive directory enumeration and one log file per failed setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Diagnostics were printed only to task output and partial import files were not enumerated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations precede the terminal throw so the partial state survives later cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query operating-system/computer CIM data, optional features, services, and reboot indicators.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new OS CIM query; the existing computer CIM query, two feature queries, four service lookups, and bounded registry checks remain once per failed import.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The OS CIM query was absent; the remaining system-state checks already ran after import failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only during terminal failure diagnosis.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover Lxss event logs and fetch at most 20 events in the import time window from each distinct discovered/fixed WSL, Host Compute, Hyper-V Compute, Worker, and VMMS log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery plus N+4 deduplicated serial event-log queries, where N is the small installed set of Lxss logs; each result is capped at 20 events. Previously there were exactly three serial fixed-log queries capped at 10 events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No event-log discovery occurred; only Lxss Operational, Hyper-V Compute, and Hyper-V Worker were queried over the preceding ten minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded diagnostic latency after failure and before the script reports failure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of installed Lxss event logs, with output capped to 20 events per distinct log; partial-file enumeration is top-level only. Realistic hosted agents expose only a small finite log set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All diagnostics are serialized by PowerShell. Event queries execute one at a time for each distinct discovered/fixed log; no concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No diagnostics are cached or coalesced, but the function is invoked once per failed setup and every result is consumed immediately. Warm-cache behavior is controlled by Windows services rather than repository code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added failure-only boundary calls and their cardinality from the changed loop and caps; low evidence that their bounded latency or allocation is large enough to constitute a regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Windows event service latency and the number of provider logs vary by runner image. However, collection occurs once on a terminal failure, is serial, and has per-log event caps, so no concrete harmful scaling mechanism is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: additional boundary fan-out is intentional, bounded, and confined to preserving diagnostics after an already terminal import failure.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced successful import and failed-import diagnostic paths. Considered output buffering/allocation and added filesystem, WSL, CIM, and event-log fan-out; all new expensive work is either negligible on success or bounded to a once-per-run terminal failure path. No valid performance finding or regression-fix record was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
